claims.text: Spark plasma sintering reduces the effective sintering temperature of powder-metallurgy high-entropy alloys relative to conventional sintering.
Inert-gas-atomized high-entropy alloy powder can be processed by spark plasma sintering.
Mechanically alloyed high-entropy alloy powders are suitable starting materials for the proposed SPS treatment.
The starting powders have preliminary loose packing or are formed into low-density compacts.
The SPS intervention employs rapid heating and plasma discharge under a controlled inert atmosphere.
SPS operates in a lower-temperature and more rapid-heating regime than traditional high-temperature, slow-heating sintering.
Localized plasma effects and rapid heating enhance mass transport and accelerate diffusion at particle interfaces.
Enhanced interfacial mass transport leads to effective densification.
Plasma discharges and rapid heating accelerate diffusion and sintering kinetics during SPS.
SPS lowers the activation energy required for densification.
Accelerated SPS kinetics reduce the overall temperature required for sintering.
SPS can produce dense bulk high-entropy alloy material.
SPS can preserve fine microstructural features without coarsening.
Comparable or improved densification and microstructure can be achieved by SPS at a significantly lower temperature than by conventional sintering.
Conventional sintering requires prolonged high-temperature treatment to achieve densification similar to SPS.
The proposed temperature-reduction effect applies broadly to powder-metallurgically processed high-entropy alloys under inert or vacuum conditions.
The magnitude of the SPS temperature reduction varies with alloy composition, powder characteristics, processing atmosphere, particle size, and SPS parameters.
